source.title: Scaling Law of Large Sequential Recommendation Models
source.authors: Gaowei Zhang; Yupeng Hou; Hong-Yu Lu; Yu Chen; W. Zhao; Ji-Rong Wen

page_placements.theme: Repeated data, finite data and stopping have capacity-dependent value

record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-law experiments to ID-based sequential recommendation models, a different training and task setting from language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own cross-entropy scaling, extrapolation, data-repetition, model-shape and downstream recommendation results. It also discusses cited language-model results, which are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws to its own test cross-entropy of ID-based sequential-recommendation transformers (98.3K–0.83B non-embedding params). It predicts the two largest models from four small ones, varies data size and model shape, and measures downstream recommendation metrics across scales. This is a new setting (recommendation, not text) with direct results on V5, plus V2, V4, V6 and V7 transposed to that setting. V1 and V3 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim the following. A fit on models under 100x smaller predicts the 0.83B model's test loss. Their exponent (0.121) is larger than in language models (0.07), and it falls with data sparsity. Larger models are more data-efficient. Repeating data helps for a few epochs. Shape at fixed N matters little, but width-only scaling fails.
record.recipe_differences: Uses decoder-only transformers for ID-based sequential recommendation and fits power laws to recommendation cross-entropy; it does not reproduce language-model pretraining experiments or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted model-size exponent varies with dataset/data sparsity; the paper reports a flatter curve as interaction data is reduced.

fits_no_version.finding: Repeating data for 2–5 epochs improves validation loss for both the 98.3K and 75.5M models. Returns diminish rapidly over 6–12 epochs and reach zero by 13–30, with overfitting in the large model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-constrained recommendation models gain from a few epochs of repetition with rapidly diminishing returns, as in data-constrained LM scaling.

record.problems: Several key scaling and task results are shown only in figures without exact values in the text. The study uses two recommendation datasets and reports no uncertainty estimates for the extracted results.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports further recommendation metrics and detailed comparisons in Table V and Figures 5–9. Only the task-level scale findings directly relevant to the listed versions are retained; separate metric values and subgroup details not stated in the text are not extracted.

untested.parts: Not tested: no language-model pretraining loss.
Not tested: no compute-budget sweep or compute-optimal allocation; compute is held 'adequate'.
Language-model runs; extrapolation beyond ~88x the largest fit model; quantitative prediction error.
Image/video modalities, fine-tuning/transfer scaling, and a power-law fit for the repeated-data regime (only loss-vs-epoch curves are shown).
A predictive fit of downstream metrics against scale or loss; the link to pretraining loss.
Parameter-counting conventions, schedules, fitting methods, compute-optimal split.
Language models; architecture details other than depth/width.

missing.what: Fitted constants EN=4.9, N0=6.8e5, αN=0.121, and the comparison to αN=0.07 for language models
NDCG also follows scaling but shows a low-return regime at 0.8B parameters
missing.locator: Section IV-A, last paragraph; Fig. 2(a) right axis

missing.what: Table V: LSRMdeep (0.83B) NDCG@10 0.2319 vs SASRec (98.3K) 0.1212 vs LSRMwide (2 layers, 34.56M) 0.0506; width-only scaling degrades performance
Training-technique ablation: without layer-wise dropout and optimizer switching, 24-layer test loss rises from 4.7182 to 4.7504

record.verdict_notes: Every scaling result is from a single MovieLens-20M fit with no uncertainty reported. Holdout agreement is visual only. The 0.83B model trains on only 18.5M interactions, so data may be its bottleneck. The record links V2, V4, V6 and V7 to recommendation models as a T3 transposition; researchers should weigh that these versions are framed for language models. Peer-review status in the record (RecSys) is not confirmed by the text.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test held-out pretraining loss of language models as a function of parameters, tokens or compute.
Tests prediction of larger ID-based recommendation models, not language-model runs; the largest recommendation model is 0.8B parameters.
No fixed-compute-budget sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is tested.
Tests transformer depth/width shape at fixed non-embedding parameter counts for recommendation models, not language models or every architecture detail.
Tests ID-based sequential recommendation and repeated-data training; does not test image/video modalities, fine-tuning or transfer as pretraining regimes.
Tests recommendation-task performance at different model scales; does not establish a relationship between downstream performance and language-model pretraining loss.
Shows dataset/data-sparsity dependence of the scaling exponent in recommendation; does not compare parameter-counting conventions, fitting methods or compute-optimal allocation laws.
